To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the liquid film is not a simple extension of the bulk liquid, but rather is a complex interface that is strongly influenced by its environment.
the ice/vapur interface is faceted at the basal and secondary prismatic plane, and is close to a critical point for the primary prismatic plane.
The liquid film at the ice/vapor interface is very thin (0.5nm) and behaves as a liquid with a density close to the bulk water density.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the premelt layer of ice.
the study of the structure of the premelt layer at the ice/water/vapour interface at the triple point using the TIP4/2005 model of water.
the structure of ice at its triple point.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ice/vapor interface is a complex interface, which can be understood in terms of the two simpler interfaces that constitute it, the ice/water interface, and the water/vapor interface.
(i) the liquid film behaves as a liquid, (ii) the liquid film does not behave as ice and (iii) the liquid film is different from bulk water.
the adsorbed layer is indeed a quasi-liquid layer and that it behaves like water.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the liquid film at the ice triple point behaves as an independent water/vapour interface at small scales, and as a complex ice/vapur interface at large scales.
the adsorbed liquid film behaves like a liquid film of water, with an additional layer of ice.
, for the TIP/4P/200 model, the liquid film of ice behaves like water and the ice/film interface behaves like ice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the liquid film of ice is not a single phase but rather is a complex interface between two distinct phases.
the liquid film behaves as an independent water surface at the smallest length scales and as an ice/vapour surface at large length scales.
the adsorbed layer at the ice/vapor interface behaves like water at large length scale and like ice at small length scale.
